Expected result: Builder starts with an empty question; course association, question order, totals, duration, pass mark, and attempts match saved input.

Expected result: Invalid inputs are blocked with feedback; no malformed exam is saved. Test each input separately.

Steps: Create an exam while C1 is draft; try as students. Publish C1; repeat as enrolled S1 and unenrolled S2.
Expected result: Instructor can prepare the draft-course assessment; students require a published course and current entitlement.

Steps: On E1, answer one 2-mark MCQ correctly, one incorrectly, and skip one; submit.
Expected result: Total 6; earned 2 minus 0.25 = 1.75; correct/wrong/skipped counts 1/1/1; 29% after rounding; Fail against pass mark 2. Blank answer receives no deduction.

Steps: On a separate equivalent exam, disable negative marking; submit the same pattern. On another, answer all incorrectly with negative marking enabled.
Expected result: No-negative score is 2/6; all-wrong score is floored at 0; score never becomes negative.

Steps: Submit E1; try again immediately; reload history. After the 24-hour cooldown, use the remaining attempt, then try exceeding 2 attempts.
Expected result: Cooldown enforced; attempt history persists; maximum-attempt limit is enforced. Until the cooldown passes, record the final portion Blocked rather than assuming success.

Steps: Create True/False and short-answer questions with a known accepted answer. Take them using correct/incorrect responses; inspect the result.
Expected result: Correct question types render; scores and explanations match the answer key. For CODE, run only a benign known-answer example in isolated staging; unsafe code execution remains a deployment blocker.

Steps: Before submission, inspect the normal exam page and its Network responses; try any visible preview route/control.
Expected result: Unsubmitted student cannot obtain correct answers, accepted-answer lists, explanations that reveal answers, or hidden code test cases through preview flags.

Steps: Start a separate short-duration exam; let the visible timer expire. Record submit/timeout behavior and then reload the page.
Expected result: UI follows its advertised timeout/submission behavior without freezing or presenting an extra attempt as the same attempt. This checks browser behavior only; server-enforced exam elapsed-time guarantees need a separate review.

Steps: At `/contests/create`, publish a permitted course/global MCQ contest with real questions and dates; open its detail page.
Expected result: Saved content, scope, audience, duration, dates, and unique URL are correct; no sample problems appear.

Steps: Try end before start, an already-ended window, duration longer than the window, and invalid/empty questions.
Expected result: Creation rejected with useful feedback; no invalid contest published.

Steps: Visit the contest before start, during the window, and at/after end. Try submitting outside the window.
Expected result: Upcoming/Live/Ended derives from actual times; submissions outside the window are denied by the server. Record times in Asia/Dhaka.

Steps: Submit known correct and incorrect MCQ answers during the live window; reopen results/history and any leaderboard.
Expected result: Result matches the answer key; submission belongs to the correct student/contest; participation/ranking reflects real submissions. Record duplicate-submit behavior for review.

Steps: Inspect active contest Network responses for solutions, then revisit home/catalog after contest ends.
Expected result: Active solutions are withheld; ended contest leaves the homepage banner but remains in the eligible catalog.

Steps: Inspect library Security settings without copying any keys.
Expected result: Embed view token authentication enabled; Basic MediaCage DRM enabled; MP4 fallback disabled; original-file exposure and Early Play disabled. This is a configuration check, not proof of successful encrypted playback.

Steps: Upload a small real lesson video through C1's lesson editor; inspect Bunny encoding status; reload the saved lesson.
Expected result: Real video is created in the configured library; upload errors are explicit; stable saved reference survives reload; playable only after provider processing permits it.

Steps: Play the private lesson in C1; pause, seek, adjust volume, enter/leave fullscreen, then reload.
Expected result: Authorized playback works without unrelated fallback media or browser exceptions. Do not infer watched progress solely from an open iframe.

Steps: Open the private lesson through the app; repeat in private browsing and with access only to C2.
Expected result: App does not issue playable private content to unauthorized viewers. A copied valid bearer embed URL may work until expiry; that alone does not prove the application access check failed.

Steps: For a fresh signed Bunny embed URL, change one token character; separately retain a copy until its actual expiry, then load it in a new session.
Expected result: Tampered and expired signed URLs cannot begin fresh playback; authorized app navigation can obtain a new valid URL. Do not publish the signed URL as evidence.

Steps: Inspect Bunny playback/network behavior and compare with VIDEO-01 settings; test current desktop Chrome and one mobile browser.
Expected result: Provider protection is active during working playback and no app MP4 fallback is exposed. Document only observed evidence; watermark, hidden download buttons, or iframe use alone do not prove encryption or prevent screen recording. External YouTube/Vimeo/public-file links are outside Bunny DRM coverage.
